conviction_note: The evidence is close to balanced. Q3 sits inside a guide the company reaffirmed on 2026-09-29, and the FY28 framework (~11% subscription growth, >=33% margin) is already public, which lowers the risk of a ServiceNow-style surprise deceleration. Against that: the Q2 beat was not passed through to the FY top end, so the implied Q4 can look light, and management promised a second-half bookings ramp that Q3 now has to show. impact_sum +0.3 and the scaled +0.17 agree in sign and are both near zero; abs_move_pct is held near the 8.8% implied move because sign uncertainty does not shrink it.
bar: Company guide (2026-08-27 Q2 release): Q3 FY27 subscription revenue $2.515B (+12%), 12-month subscription backlog (cRPO) growth 11-12%, non-GAAP operating margin 30.0%; FY27 subscription $9.940-9.950B (+13%), non-GAAP operating margin 31.0%. Guidance reiterated in the 2026-09-29 8-K (except GAAP operating margin). https://investor.workday.com/news-and-events/press-releases/news-details/2026/Workday-Announces-Fiscal-2027-Second-Quarter-Financial-Results/default.aspx . Street: total revenue ~$2.69B and non-GAAP EPS $2.74 from both Zacks (https://www.nasdaq.com/articles/wday-q2-earnings-beat-estimates-subscription-growth-margin-gains context; Q3 consensus quoted in https://finviz.com/news/423401/workdays-promised-second-half-ai-bookings-surge-faces-its-first-real-test) and Earnings Whispers (2026-11-16), which puts the whisper at $2.83. The bar is sourced to the company guide and two agreeing estimate sources, so no cap applies. FY28 framework from Analyst Day 2026-10-14: ~11% subscription growth (~$11B), non-GAAP operating margin >=33% (https://www.saasrise.com/news/workday-sets-11b-subscription-target-ai-arr-hits-600m-073765bd-1771-41f7-b667-e74386223ed7).
positioning_check: Short interest at the 2026-10-30 FINRA settlement was 11.75M shares, about 4.9% of shares outstanding, with 5.37 days to cover. It has fallen from 14.1M on 2026-09-15 (equibles, https://equibles.com/stocks/wday/short-interest, read 2026-11-24). The 2026-11-13 settlement is published today and was not available. This is not a crowded short. 25-delta skew is +2.86 vol points (moderate; downside paid). ATM IV is 110.8% on the 11-27 expiry, the event-implied move 8.8%, put/call OI 1.04. 20-day run-up is -10.66% and the stock is 21.45% off its 52-week high, after a 5% sympathy drop on 2026-10-29 (ServiceNow -19%) and -5.8% on 2026-11-17 in an application-software sell-off. Earnings Whispers calls sentiment 'bearish but softer than prior quarter'.

findings.finding: Workday has beaten its own subscription guide by about 0.65% (Q2 FY27: $2.471B against a $2.455B guide). The same cadence on the $2.515B Q3 guide gives about $2.53B, and Q2's 31.1% non-GAAP margin beat its guide too. Q3's 30.0% margin guide is below Q2's 31.1%, so a margin beat is likely.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 FY27 (2026-08-27): subscription beat plus margin raise, +5.76%. Q1 FY27 (2026-05-21): beat, best Q1 net new ACV in five years, +5.16%. Q3 FY26 (2025-11-25): beat with a soft outlook, -7.85%. Beats are paid only when the guide holds.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced. A routine small beat inside the guided range is what the street models. If the market doubted the quarter itself, the Q3 consensus would sit below the $2.69B total guide, and it sits on it.
findings.independence: Q1 release (https://investor.workday.com/news-and-events/press-releases/news-details/2026/Workday-Announces-Fiscal-2027-First-Quarter-Financial-Results/default.aspx, 2026-05-21) shows the same pattern: subscription $2.354B, +14.3%. Same company, so the source family is the same.

findings.finding: On 2026-09-29, two months into the three-month Q3, Workday filed an 8-K (Item 2.02) reiterating its Q3 and FY27 guidance except GAAP operating margin. In the same filing it cut about 2.5% of its workforce (Item 2.05; $65-80M total charges, $55-70M of them in Q3, GAAP only). The company had two of three months of Q3 data when it reaffirmed, and the cost action supports the non-GAAP margin.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The baseline counts the 2026-09-29 8-K as a 'print' with a +0.68% reaction, so the reaffirmation itself moved little. Restructuring charges are excluded from the non-GAAP line the stock trades on.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced, because it is public and lands inside the guide. What it removes is a bottom-line Q3 miss. If the market feared a Q3 miss, the implied move would sit well above the 5.5% median reaction rather than at 8.8%, and the skew would be steeper than +2.86.
findings.independence: Analyst Day 2026-10-14 (https://quartr.com/events/workday-inc-wday-analyst-day-2026_3YjWCEc5) gave no warning and reported AI ARR of about $600M. That is a different event from the same company.

findings.finding: The FY28 framework is already public: about 11% subscription growth (~$11B) and a non-GAAP operating margin of at least 33%. It was given at the Q2 call and the 2026-10-14 Analyst Day, and Q3 cRPO was guided to decelerate to 11-12% from 14.2% (about one point is the Paradox lap). Unlike ServiceNow on 2026-10-29, Workday has already told the market about its deceleration, so tonight's call is less likely to reveal a new one.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Guidance resets drove the big moves: -12.52% (2025-05-22) and -7.85% (2025-11-25) on soft outlooks, and the Feb 2026 FY27 guide was sold in extended trading. Where the guide held (2026-05-21, 2026-08-27) the stock rose about 5%.
findings.why_not_priced: The framework itself is priced. What may not be priced is the read-across: WDAY fell 5% in sympathy with ServiceNow's cRPO-deceleration drop on 2026-10-29 and is down 10.7% over 20 days. That treats the two the same, though Workday's deceleration is pre-announced. If the market had separated them, WDAY would not have lagged the 3.0% sub-industry median on 2026-11-17 (it fell 5.8%).
findings.independence: The Q2 FY27 call transcript (https://www.webull.com/news/15497663744238592, 2026-08-27) has the CFO saying the FY28 target is 'consistent with our expected second half FY 2027 growth rate of approximately 11%' and that 'not all of that has been factored into our FY 2028 outlook'. Same company, a different document.

findings.finding: Arithmetic on the guide: Q1 $2.354B + Q2 $2.471B + Q3 guide $2.515B = $7.340B. That leaves an implied Q4 of $2.600-2.610B inside the FY27 range of $9.940-9.950B. In August, the Q2 beat ($16M) raised only the low end and left the top unchanged, so the second half was trimmed. If a Q3 beat again does not flow to the FY top end, the implied Q4 and the cRPO guide read as a deceleration below the ~11% second-half rate. That is the line the stock fell on in Nov 2025.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: 2025-11-25: Q3 beat with a growth outlook that 'fails to excite investors', -7.85%. 2025-05-22: -12.52%. A Q4 guide that only holds has been sold.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: skew of +2.86 pays for downside and the preview names a cautious Q4 outlook as the risk. Nobody has priced it fully, because the consensus total revenue still assumes the guide is met. If it were fully priced, the stock would already trade at the framework's growth multiple, and the skew would be far steeper.
findings.independence: Q2 release (https://investor.workday.com/news-and-events/press-releases/news-details/2026/Workday-Announces-Fiscal-2027-Second-Quarter-Financial-Results/default.aspx) and Q1 release, same company. The arithmetic rests on those documents.

findings.finding: Management set its own bar for this quarter: on the Q2 call it said the 'back half of the year looks really positive' and that Flex Credit signings would 'significantly grow' in H2. Only about 300 Flex Credit agreements exist (about 200 signed in Q2), and the revenue is said to land mostly in FY28. Q3 is the first test, but the money from those bookings may not show in subscription revenue or cRPO yet.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: AI metrics have not moved this stock on their own. Agentic ARR of about $600M at Analyst Day was followed by a weaker stock into November.
findings.why_not_priced: The promise is public, but how big the bookings must be to satisfy it is not, so there is no number to price it against. If the market believed a bookings surge, the stock would not be down 10.7% into the print with downside paid.
findings.independence: Earnings Whispers preview, 2026-11-16 (https://finviz.com/news/423401/workdays-promised-second-half-ai-bookings-surge-faces-its-first-real-test), frames Q3 as the 'first real test'. It interprets the same call, so the two are not independent.

findings.finding: The drawdown into the print came from the sector, not the company. On 2026-10-29 WDAY fell 5% when ServiceNow fell 19% on its cRPO guide. On 2026-11-17 WDAY fell 5.8% (sub-industry median -3.0%) in a software sell-off with no Workday news, which 57 of 62 application-software names joined. Short interest fell from 14.1M (09-15) to 11.75M (10-30), 4.9% of shares outstanding. The stock enters at $183.56, 10.7% below its level 20 days ago.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: After the drawdown into the Feb 2026 print, the guide was still sold (-6.69% on the 2026-02-04 8-K). After the Q1 FY27 lows (52-week low $112.50 on 2026-04-10), an in-line guide bought +5.16%.
findings.why_not_priced: Positioning is by definition in the price. The finding is that the recent loss was sector beta rather than company news, which lowers the bar for an in-line guide. The skew is only +2.86, not extreme, so the option market is not strongly short this name.
findings.independence: Short interest series, equibles (https://equibles.com/stocks/wday/short-interest). ServiceNow sympathy move: 247wallst, 2026-11-02 (https://247wallst.com/investing/2026/11/02/servicenow-has-become-the-canary-in-the-coal-mine-for-agentic-ai-driven-software-implosion/).

findings.finding: Workday priced $2.5B of senior notes on 2026-10-21 (closed 10-23): 5.700% 2029, 6.000% 2031, 6.300% 2033 and 6.500% 2036. The proceeds retire the $1.0B 3.500% notes due April 2027, and the remaining ~$1.5B goes to general corporate purposes. Buybacks of $5.23B ran above FCF of $2.84B over the four quarters to July 2026, and cash fell to $3.4B from $8.19B. On this reading the money buys a refinancing plus continued buybacks, not a ramp. Higher coupons on more debt add a small interest drag to non-GAAP EPS from Q4.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior print turned on financing. The $4.0B buyback authorization added in Aug 2026 went with a +5.76% day, but alongside a beat.
findings.why_not_priced: It is public and small, a refinancing plus buyback funding. Its only path to the print is the FY27 EPS and interest-expense line, which few previews model. If it were seen as distress, credit spreads and the skew would show it; the notes priced at investment-grade coupons.
findings.independence: Trefis bear case, 2026-11-19 (https://www.trefis.com/stock/wday/articles/626861/what-would-a-short-seller-say-about-workday/2026-11-19), gives the buyback-over-FCF gap and the cash decline.

findings.finding: Enterprise application demand at counterparties and competitors is not deteriorating. SAP's Q3 2026 current cloud backlog was €24.1B, +28% (+26% constant currency), including SuccessFactors, Workday's direct HCM competitor. Paycom (2026-11-04) beat and raised its 2026 revenue guide. ServiceNow's cRPO grew 20.5%; it was the forward guide, not demand, that sank that stock.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Peer prints have moved WDAY in sympathy (-5% on 2026-10-29). Workday's own print has not tracked peer strength reliably.
findings.why_not_priced: A peer proxy, and public. SAP sells to the same large-enterprise HCM buyers but its backlog is mostly ERP/S4 migration, so the read-across to Workday is weak. If the market read peer demand into WDAY, WDAY would not have traded with the seat-pricing worries instead of with SAP's beat.
findings.independence: Paycom Q3 2026 (https://zacks.com/stock/news/3024394/paycom-q3-earnings-beat-estimates-on-revenue-growth-margin-gains, 2026-11-04). ServiceNow Q3 2026 release (https://investor.servicenow.com/news/news-details/2026/ServiceNow-Reports-Third-Quarter-2026-Financial-Results/default.aspx). All are proxies; none is a Workday counterparty statement.

findings.finding: The seat-compression worry is not visible in the layoff series. Challenger counted 43,994 announced US job cuts in October 2026, the fewest for the month since 2023 and down 71% year on year. AI was cited for only 1,265 cuts, the year's low, against 38,579 in May 2026. Workday's per-employee pricing is exposed to customer headcount.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: There is no measured link between Workday's prints and the macro layoff series. Management said seat counts at existing customers are roughly flat.
findings.why_not_priced: A macro proxy, public and broad. Workday has not confirmed that it transmits to the company, and low layoffs with low hiring still means flat seats, so the effect is small either way.
findings.independence: https://tradingeconomics.com/united-states/challenger-job-cuts/news/598602 reports the same Challenger release, so it is the same underlying data.

outside_window.finding: The Galileo agent (Josh Bersin Company) integrated into Sana Enterprise reaches general availability in February 2027, and the new Sana home screen reaches GA in early 2027. Any monetisation falls after this window.
The $1.0B 3.500% notes due 2027-04-01 are to be retired with the October proceeds. Interest savings and costs land in FY28.

searched_and_found_nothing: A Workday 8-K dated 2026-10-01 is listed on the IR site; I found no content for it and no executive change on that date.
Customer-win press releases ('selects Workday') for Aug-Oct 2026: none found.
A dated, current-cycle analyst downgrade or upgrade in November 2026: none confirmed. The KeyBanc and Piper items found were undated or from 2025.
Street consensus for 12-month backlog (cRPO) and the Q4 subscription number: not found in free sources.
Share-price reaction to the 2026-10-14 Analyst Day: not found.

rejected_candidates.detail: I could not confirm a date for either downgrade from the search snippets. The related Yahoo article fetched was a 2025 Piper Sandler downgrade, so these may also be a year old.

rejected_candidates.detail: Dated 2025-07-10, so it is not current evidence. The theme is already covered by the seat-compression and positioning findings.

rejected_candidates.detail: A Q2 item with no path into Q3; it is part of the same Q2 release behind the beat-cadence finding.

baseline_tension: The findings net slightly positive (+0.3) against a moderate downside skew (+2.86) and a -10.7% run-up. The run-up supports the small positive, because the decline was sector beta. The skew pushes p_up back toward 50, so I hold p_up at 51 rather than higher.
lessons_applied: Rules 1 and 6 (inside the guide): the beat-cadence finding went from +0.3 to +0.2 and the 09-29 reaffirmation from +0.5 to +0.3, because both land inside a guide the company already gave.
Rule 1 (a verified fact is not a predicted reaction): the FY28-framework read-across went from +0.5 to +0.4; it infers a reaction rather than reporting a document number.
Rule 7 (positioning against skew): the sector-drawdown positioning finding went from +0.5 to +0.3, because its sign runs against a +2.86 downside skew; short interest was checked and is not crowded.
Rule 4 (financing is a question): I asked what the notes buy (a refinancing plus buybacks, not distress), and the -0.1 stood.
Rule 5 (proxies small, not dropped): the peer and Challenger proxies stayed at +0.2 and +0.1.
The scaled number moved with these changes: p_up went from 52 to 51 and abs_move_pct stayed at 8.5, so expected_move_pct went from +0.34 to +0.17.
